title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hook and quality gating
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: our existing eval-harness CI gates run per-suite quality checks which can miss regressions that only affect a small subset of critical prompts. This PR introduces a per-prompt regression CI hook and a lightweight quality gating layer so regressions on prioritized prompt-sets (billing, auth, safety) fail CI quickly and surface actionable diffs.

What this change does: adds a new eval-harness subcommand `ci-check --per-prompt` and a configurable hook that integrates with our GitHub Actions pipeline. The hook compares per-prompt metrics (exact-match, rouge-L, semantic-similarity) against stored baselines and a configurable acceptance window. If any prioritized prompt exceeds the regression threshold, the CI job fails and emits a summarized artifact with the top-10 regressions and example responses.

Implementation notes: the PR introduces: (1) tests/fixtures/prompt-baselines/{billing,auth,safety}.json (baseline metrics + metadata), (2) eval_harness/ci_hooks/per_prompt_hook.py (core comparison and reporting), (3) eval_harness/cli.py changes to expose `ci-check` flags and a --report-path output, (4) a lightweight JSON artifact format (per_prompt_report.json) for downstream ingestion by the Console/alerts pipeline, and (5) GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/eval-ci.yml` addition that runs `pytest -q` and `python -m eval_harness.ci_hooks.per_prompt_hook --per-prompt --report-path=./artifacts/per_prompt_report.json` on PRs touching `models/`, `prompts/`, or `eval-harness/`.

Backward compatibility and rollout: the default regression threshold is conservative (5% relative drop on semantic-similarity or a delta of 0.05 absolute on normalized scores) and only applies to prompt-sets labeled as `critical` in the baseline files. Non-critical prompt regressions are reported but do not fail the job. This allows gradual adoption and reduces CI noise. We added an opt-in config in `.eval-harness/config.yml` to toggle strict mode for teams that want CI-blocking behavior for more prompt sets.

Testing and validation: added unit tests covering hook logic and a small e2e smoke test that runs the hook against a synthetic baseline to ensure regressions are detected and the artifact is produced. Local run instructions included in the PR description: `python -m eval_harness.ci_hooks.per_prompt_hook --per-prompt --baseline tests/fixtures/prompt-baselines/billing.json --predictions tests/fixtures/predictions/billing_preds.json --report-path ./out.json`.

Observability and alerts: per_prompt_report.json contains per-prompt metric deltas and top-k example pairs. The Console ingestion job (separate PR planned) will consume these artifacts to create per-prompt alerts and surface regressions on dashboards. For now, CI job logs print a short table of the top regressions and attach the full artifact.

Notes on performance: hook runs are lightweight — comparisons operate on aggregated metrics and limit sample size to N=256 examples per prompt by default. Measured addition to CI runtime on a representative run was +28s avg (median) on GitHub-hosted runners.

Related work: references ENG-4823 (per-prompt gating thesis) and ENG-4890 (console ingestion contract). Also follows patterns from previous eval-harness CI hooks (see pr-221501 and pr-314159 for history).

Checklist:
- [x] Add per-prompt hook implementation
- [x] Add baseline fixtures and config schema
- [x] Add unit + smoke tests
- [x] Add GH Actions workflow entry
- [x] Add docs snippet in eval-harness/README.md

Next steps: follow-up PR will add Console ingestion and alert routing, plus an RFC to standardize artifact schema across repos.

review_comments: Jordan Lee: Can you add a short explanation of the baseline format in the README? Right now it's a bit terse.
Aisha Patel: Added README snippet and example baseline files. Also included validation in the hook to catch malformed baselines.
Priya Nair: Is the default 5% threshold going to be noisy for language-generation prompts? Can we allow per-prompt override?
Aisha Patel: Good call — added `threshold` override in the baseline schema so critical prompts can have custom thresholds. Updated unit test to cover override behavior.
Evan Chen: Small nit — the GH workflow should only run the heavy hook when files under `prompts/` or `models/` change. Otherwise this will run on all PRs.
Aisha Patel: Updated workflow to only trigger on `paths` that include `prompts/**`, `models/**`, or `eval-harness/**`.
Jordan Lee: CI flaked on macOS runner once, reran and passed. Approving after green CI.
Priya Nair: Approve — this will help catch subtle regressions we miss today.
release_notes: Add per-prompt CI gating: new eval-harness `ci-check --per-prompt` hook, baseline format for critical prompt-sets, conservative default thresholds, and GH Actions integration. Opt-in strict mode available via .eval-harness/config.yml.
notes: Follow-up: console ingestion PR to consume per_prompt_report.json (ENG-4890)
Rollout plan: enable on core repos for 2 weeks in reporting-only mode, then flip strict=true for critical prompts if noise is low
